reviewer.method: Independent full-film re-review of the 43-shot (shot-0..shot-42) B1 render after the content revision covering scenes 1-4, 7, 8, 10 and 12 (commit caf83f4, duration 182.587s -> 192.375s). Method: (1) read output/film-reference/evidence.json and review-template.json for the authoritative current shot list, frame_index/source_time and the 7 required checks; (2) read project.json in full for every shot's layer/keyframe data, and cross-referenced project.json's own 'metadata.scenes' outline (scene/title/phase/shot/start/end/scale) to get the authoritative scene<->shot-id mapping, since this is ground truth rather than inferred; (3) located every content change named in the critique (scene1 opening line + metronome, scene2 search label, scene3 sticky-note captions, scene4 claim card, scene7 problem-statement restructure, scene8 checkmark label + dialogue extension, scene10 timestamp line + dialogue extension + motion-gap fix, scene12 new summary page + compressed task card) by grepping project.json for its literal new/changed text and by diffing project.json between commit caf83f4~1 and HEAD (and reading commit caf83f4's own message), rather than trusting the shot numbers given in the task brief. CORRECTION TO THE TASK BRIEF: the brief's claim that shot-ids shifted by +1 from shot-19 onward (because scene 12 gained a shot) does not hold. Direct comparison of findings-film-v2.json's shot-by-shot content descriptions (42 shots, shot-0..shot-41) against the current 43-shot structure, plus the project.json git diff, shows shots 0-40 are unchanged in index/order/content-mapping (only their absolute timestamps shifted, because scenes 1/8/10 grew longer); the only structural change is that the former single shot-41 (task card, 6.0s) was split into a new shot-41 (brand-new 'Halaman rencana Vidka' summary page, 3.0s) followed by a new shot-42 (the same task card, now compressed to 3.0s). So the actual new/changed-content shots are: shot-24 (scene 7 hold, NOT shot-19/20 as the brief guessed), shot-26+shot-27 (scene 8 talk2+hold, NOT shot-22/23), shot-32/33/34+shot-35 (scene 10 talk1-3+hold, NOT shot-29-31), and shot-41+shot-42 (scene 12, roughly matching the brief's guess). Scenes 1-4's changed shots (0-4, 5, 9, 13) do match the brief's numbers. (4) For every shot with new/changed content, extracted start/mid/end and additional in-between frames from output/film.mp4 with ffmpeg at the shot's exact absolute source_time windows, read them, and for scene 10's motion-gap fix additionally stepped frames every 0.2-0.5s across 154.2-158.6s absolute (both the removed-gap window and beyond) to directly confirm visible, gradual pixel-level motion rather than trusting the edited keyframe numbers. Zoomed crops (PIL) were used to inspect shot-41's header-vs-ring-band collision at full detail. (5) For shots not touched by this revision, confirmed via project.json's scene outline that their total scene duration and internal content are byte-identical to the pre-revision cut (verified for scenes 5/6/9/11 and the untouched shots of scenes 2/3/4/8/10/12), then did representative frame spot-checks (shot-0, shot-5, shot-9, shot-13, shot-17 end, shot-22 early, shot-25, shot-32, shot-33) to confirm the render genuinely matches, rather than assuming identity from timestamps alone. Shots 0-13 (scenes 1-4) were additionally cross-checked against review/preview-review-v9.json, which already independently reviewed and approved this exact sample (98/98, 0 blocking) against the current bounds. Findings-film-v2.json's own pre-existing non-blocking defects (shot-17 typography_captions residual ring-overlap flash; shot-22 contact_continuity notebook/ring-vs-chin overlap) were spot-checked frame-by-frame and confirmed still present unchanged, so they are carried forward as 'unmet' rather than silently dropped or re-litigated. (6) Checked audio: per-segment volumedetect across all 4 new/extended TTS regions (scene1 opening line, scene8 Herry extension, scene10 both Herry lines) confirms healthy, non-silent, non-clipping levels; whole-film loudnorm analysis measures -20.2 LUFS integrated / -1.8 dBTP true peak, consistent with the previously-approved -20.3 LUFS baseline. One genuine blocking finding was identified: shot-41 (the brand-new 'Halaman rencana Vidka' summary page) reintroduces the ring-band/header text collision for its full 3.0s duration, confirmed by zoomed pixel inspection, not a one-frame artifact.

blocking_issues: shot-41 (scene 12, 'Halaman rencana Vidka' summary page, absolute 186.376-189.375s): the new red header text sits directly across the notebook's spiral-ring band for the shot's entire 3.0s duration, with three ring loops visibly crossing through its letterforms (zoomed crop confirms this at 186.4s, 188.1s, 189.0s and 189.3s -- i.e. throughout the shot, not a transient frame). This is a regression of the ring-overlap typography/composition fault that was identified and fixed in shots 14, 16, 17 and 25 of the pre-revision full-film review (the fix pattern there was to keep headers at y=100+ with the notebook's rings ending by y~170-180; this shot's notebook sits higher, at y=60, with its header placed at y=90, squarely inside the ring band). Recommended fix: raise the header to clear the rings (e.g. move the notebook down or the header up/outside the ring band), following the same pattern already used successfully elsewhere in the film.
